question: The EU’s multi-annual financial allocation for Palestine under the European Joint Strategy 2021-2024 amounts to EUR 1.177 billion, a large share of which is direct financial or cash support to the Palestinian Authority (PA). The PA rewards families of political prisoners and terrorists with monthly payments.

The more serious the crime, the higher the reward to the family, which can reach the equivalent of several thousand euros. The World Bank has described such payments as ‘not [ ... ] justified from a welfare or fiscal perspective’. More than 60 EU nationals have been killed by Palestinian terrorists since 7 October 2023.

In January 2024, the PA added 3 550 prisoners and 23 210 so-called ‘martyrs’ to its lists, guaranteeing that the PA would ‘provide the services that it gives these families’. Some – possibly all – of the terrorists responsible for the killing of 60 EU nationals are among these prisoners and martyrs. Given the fungibility of money (i.e.

the perfectly interchangeability of individual units of money), how can the Commission explain to EU taxpayers that the EU is financing a government (the PA) that rewards terror, thereby also supporting the even more despicable incentive of a higher reward for deadlier attacks?
answer: The EU has never contributed to the ‘allowance scheme’ of the Palestinian Authority (PA). The Commission’s extended screening vetting system ensure that no EU funding goes to the beneficiaries of the Prisoners Fund, the detainees and families of perpetrators of terrorist attacks.

Through PEGASE (Méchanisme Palestino-européen de Gestion de l’Aide Socio-économique), the EU has safeguards in place to protect EU funds provided against misuse or deviation for unintended purposes. Every individual recipient of EU funds and every invoice to reimburse medical expenditures is screened through available tools.

PEGASE also includes some additional checks of indirect beneficiaries of the Civil Servants and Pensioners (CSP) programme. The vetting system of beneficiaries also takes into consideration the lists of detainees, families of perpetrators of terrorist attacks and security staff when conducting the eligibility assessment.

Beneficiaries of allowances for detainees and their families provided by the PA are categorically excluded from any payment made through PEGASE. This mechanism has been assessed thoroughly as part of the Review (1) of ongoing financial assistance for Palestine (2), which details the thorough mechanism of screening of the beneficiaries.
